about: Statements typed by hand from public sources on the stations of Luch (Olymp-K, 40258) and Luch 2 (Olymp-K 2, 55841) beside other operators' satellites in the geostationary belt. In the belt every object shares the plane, so the stages a source states are beside (the day it arrived at the slot), closest (in kilometres) and left; alsoNear lists co-located satellites a detector may name instead. The CSIS data repository's windows are its 'nearest neighbour within 0.075 degrees for at least a week'; Langbroek's dates are the days the satellite stabilised, read from the public elements. Never derived by a program.

statements.ref: Thomas G. Roberts, "Unusual Behavior in GEO: Luch (Olymp-K)", CSIS Aerospace Security Project data repository, last updated 1 September 2022
statements.quote: nearest neighbour within 0.075 degrees for at least a week
statements.note: Luch began its westward drift about 4 April 2015. Langbroek's table has it stabilised on 26 June 2015 at 18.1 W beside Intelsat 901; SWF dates the stop 25 June.
